text.content: Trevi Health is a healthcare staffing agency based in Milan. They place nurses, physiotherapists, and specialist care workers in hospitals, private clinics, and home-care settings across northern Italy. Their operations team runs on a mix of email, spreadsheets, and a lightly customised CRM. They have no AI agents in production.

rich_text.plain_text: Trevi Health is a healthcare staffing agency based in Milan. They place nurses, physiotherapists, and specialist care workers in hospitals, private clinics, and home-care settings across northern Italy. Their operations team runs on a mix of email, spreadsheets, and a lightly customised CRM. They have no AI agents in production.

text.content: Their operations director, Marco, has been tasked with evaluating whether an AI agent could reduce the time their coordinators spend answering routine queries from two sources: candidate workers (asking about shift availability, pay rates, document requirements, and placement status) and client facilities (asking about candidate CVs, availability windows, compliance documentation, and invoicing). Both groups contact Trevi through the same shared inbox.

rich_text.plain_text: Their operations director, Marco, has been tasked with evaluating whether an AI agent could reduce the time their coordinators spend answering routine queries from two sources: candidate workers (asking about shift availability, pay rates, document requirements, and placement status) and client facilities (asking about candidate CVs, availability windows, compliance documentation, and invoicing). Both groups contact Trevi through the same shared inbox.

text.content: Marco has put together an initial brief: one agent, one inbox, handle everything. His team's feedback after a two-week prototype is that the agent does well on candidate queries and poorly on facility queries — and occasionally mixes up tone, occasionally shares candidate information with facility contacts.
